en.title: Verstappen and Lawson receive one-place grid penalties after Mexico City collision
en.dek: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson were each given a one-place grid drop for a collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
facts: Verstappen and Lawson each received a one-place grid penalty, according to Sky Sports.
The collision occurred at Turn 14 in second practice, as reported by Sky Sports.
Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and clumsy, as stated by the stewards, according to Sky Sports.
Stewards escalated the penalty from a warning to a grid drop because they had warned team managers earlier on Friday about overtaking in the final sector, according to CNA.
body: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson each received a one-place grid penalty for a collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, according to Sky Sports. The collision occurred at Turn 14 after Lawson held his ground and the pair went side by side, as reported by Sky Sports. Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and clumsy, as stated by the stewards, according to Sky Sports.

Stewards escalated the penalty from a formal warning to a grid drop because they had warned team managers earlier on Friday about overtaking in the final sector, according to CNA. They noted similar incidents this year between drivers in free practice, prompting the decision, as reported by CNA.

The incident involved two drivers from Red Bull, with Racing Bulls considered Red Bull's junior squad, as reported by Sky Sports. Lawson's future for 2027 remains uncertain, with Racing Bulls yet to confirm their driver line-up, according to Sky Sports.
Lewis Hamilton suffered a technical failure during the same practice session, causing a virtual safety car, as reported by ABC. The incident prompted a red flag to clear debris, according to ABC.
en.context: Formula One drivers practice on the track before qualifying and races. Incidents in practice can lead to penalties from stewards. The Mexico City Grand Prix is part of the 2026 season.
en.imageCaption: Charles Leclerc was the fastest of all drivers on Friday in Mexico City. ( Reuters: Eloisa Sanchez )
